name: dev.ucp.shopping.subscription_management
title: Subscription
description: Subscription management capability: lets a Platform show a buyer their subscriptions and pause, resume, skip an order of, or cancel one.

platform_schema.title: Platform Subscription Management Config
platform_schema.description: Platform configuration for this capability in a platform profile. Same shape as the capability-wide `config.webhook` proposed in #938.

webhook.description: Subscription to subscription events. Omit to poll with Get Subscription instead.

url.description: HTTPS URL where the Business delivers signed subscription events.

events.description: Event types the Platform subscribes to. When omitted, every event type the Business sends for this capability.

platform_webhook.title: Platform Webhook
platform_webhook.description: Where and which subscription events the Platform receives.

business_schema.title: Business Subscription Management Config
business_schema.description: Business configuration for this capability in a business profile.

webhook.description: The events the Business sends. A Business without it sends none, and Platforms poll.

events.description: Event types the Business sends for this capability.

business_webhook.title: Business Webhook
business_webhook.description: Which subscription events the Business sends.

event.title: Subscription Event
event.description: Thin notification that a subscription changed. Same envelope as the capability event proposed in #938: it carries identifiers and hints, and the Platform reads current state with Get Subscription.

occurred_at.description: RFC 3339 date-time when the change was committed.

revision.description: The subscription's `revision` after the change. A Platform that already holds it can skip the read.

changed.description: Hints at what changed, so a Platform can decide whether to tell the buyer. Well-known values: `status`, `upcoming_orders`, `terms`, `operations`. Not exhaustive; the read is authoritative.

order_id.description: ID of the Order the Business placed, when the change is a recurring order being placed. From then on, that Order is the Order capability's concern.

event_data.title: Subscription Event Data
event_data.description: Identifiers and hints about the change. Carries no other subscription data.

subscription.description: The subscription as it stands after the operation.

policies.description: Policies governing the subscription, including the `dev.ucp.shopping.policy.subscription` policy covering each line. `applies_to` targets are relative to the response root (e.g. `$.subscription.line_items[0]`).

messages.description: Messages about the subscription. A warning with `presentation: "disclosure"` whose `path` names an operation states what performing it means for the buyer, and is presented before the operation is requested.

revision.description: The subscription's `revision` as the buyer last saw it. The Business applies the operation only if it is still current.

upcoming_order_id.description: `id` of the entry in `upcoming_orders` the operation applies to.

list_request.description: Request for the authenticated buyer's subscriptions, optionally filtered.

status.description: Return only subscriptions in one of these `status` values.

order_id.description: Return only subscriptions whose `origin.order_id` is this Order.

filters.description: Filters, combined with AND. Omitted filters match every subscription.

subscriptions.description: Subscriptions matching the request, most recently started first.

policies.description: Policies governing the listed subscriptions. `applies_to` targets are relative to the response root (e.g. `$.subscriptions[0].line_items[0]`).

messages.description: Messages about the listed subscriptions, targeted by `path`.

reason.description: The buyer's reason for cancelling, in their words. Optional: the Business MUST NOT require it or make cancellation depend on it.
